Topics · Is there a God?

Does God command what is good, or make it good?

Plato's old question stopped Muslim theologians too. It has a third answer, and that answer has its limit.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَإِذَا فَعَلُوا۟ فَـٰحِشَةً قَالُوا۟ وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَآ ءَابَآءَنَا وَٱللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا ۗ قُلْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَأْمُرُ بِٱلْفَحْشَآءِ ۖ أَتَقُولُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when they commit an immorality, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allāh has ordered us to do it." Say, "Indeed, Allāh does not order immorality. Do you say about Allāh that which you do not know?"

Quran · Al-A'raf 7:28

Translation

For the wisdom of the Lord is great. He is mighty in power, and sees all things. His eyes are upon those who fear him. He knows every act of man. He has not commanded any man to be ungodly. He has not given any man license to sin.

Original · Ancient Greek

Ὅτι πολλὴ σοφία τοῦ Κυρίου, ἰσχυρὸς ἐν δυναστείᾳ καὶ βλέπων τὰ πάντα. Καὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς φοβουμένους αὐτὸν, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπιγνώσεται πᾶν ἔργον ἀνθρώπου. Καὶ οὐκ ἐνετείλατο οὐδενὶ ἀσεβεῖν, καὶ οὐκ ἔδωκεν ἄνεσιν οὐδενὶ ἁμαρτάνειν.

Sirach · 15:18-20

World English Bible

The dilemma is strong. If a thing is good only because it is commanded, then cruelty would be good if it were commanded, and 'God is good' says nothing. If it is commanded because it is good, then goodness stands apart from God and we can go straight to it. This text refuses the first horn. People defending something vile said that God commanded it. The reply is: God does not command indecency. That reply makes little sense if whatever He says becomes decent by His saying it.

A question for you

Which horn troubles you more?

If you sayThat goodness would be arbitrary.
ThenThen you hold that goodness has content, which is what the sentence itself assumes.
If you sayThat goodness would be independent of God.
ThenThat is what many classical theologians feared. The third answer tries to meet it.
If you sayNeither troubles me. There is no God.
ThenThen your question is what makes goodness good without God.

Part 2 of 3

﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَٱلْإِحْسَـٰنِ وَإِيتَآئِ ذِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَيَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ وَٱلْبَغْىِ ۚ يَعِظُكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, Allāh orders justice and good conduct and giving [help] to relatives and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded.

Quran · An-Nahl 16:90

Translation

Therefore turn to your God. Keep kindness and justice, and wait continually for your God.

Original · Hebrew

וְאַתָּ֖ה בֵּאלֹהֶ֣יךָ תָשׁ֑וּב חֶ֤סֶד וּמִשְׁפָּט֙ שְׁמֹ֔ר וְקַוֵּ֥ה אֶל־אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ תָּמִֽיד׃

Hosea · 12:6

World English Bible

Look at what is actually commanded here: justice, kindness, giving to those near you; and what is forbidden: indecency, wrongdoing, oppression. These are not arbitrary rules like a password. A reader can recognise them as good. So the commands appeal to something the listener can already see. A law can do that without inventing what it points to. So the command is not what creates moral worth. It calls people to it. That counts against the first horn. The second is still open.

A question for you

If people know what is good, why would they need a command?

If you sayThey don't.
ThenPerhaps not for the basics. The question remains when the good goes against what a person wants, or when people differ.
If you sayAs a reminder when we forget.
ThenThat is close to the book's name for itself: a reminder.
If you sayBecause a command has authority that knowledge lacks.
ThenThat is the next question: where does the authority come from?

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَإِذَا جَآءَكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا فَقُلْ سَلَـٰمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ ۖ كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ ۖ أَنَّهُۥ مَنْ عَمِلَ مِنكُمْ سُوٓءًۢا بِجَهَـٰلَةٍ ثُمَّ تَابَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَنَّهُۥ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when those come to you who believe in Our verses, say, "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy: that any of you who does wrong out of ignorance and then repents after that and corrects himself - indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful."

Quran · Al-An'am 6:54

Translation

Tell them, ‘“As I live,” says the Lord Yahweh, “I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live. Turn, turn from your evil ways! For why will you die, house of Israel?”’

Original · Hebrew

אֱמֹ֨ר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם חַי־אָ֣נִי ׀ נְאֻ֣ם ׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אִם־אֶחְפֹּץ֙ בְּמ֣וֹת הָרָשָׁ֔ע כִּ֣י אִם־בְּשׁ֥וּב רָשָׁ֛ע מִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ וְחָיָ֑ה שׁ֣וּבוּ שׁ֜וּבוּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֧ם הָרָעִ֛ים וְלָ֥מָּה תָמ֖וּתוּ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

Ezekiel · 33:11

World English Bible

So here is the third answer, held by many theists. Good is not above God, and it is not a whim. It is rooted in what God is. He commands justice because He is just, and He writes mercy on Himself: this sentence says so. So the standard is neither outside Him nor arbitrary. The objection comes at once: why call His nature good? Isn't that the same dilemma, one level up? That reply is serious. All accounts end somewhere. This one ends in a Living Good.

A question for you

What do you make of the third answer?

If you sayIt moves the question without solving it.
ThenThat is the strongest objection. Whether any account does more stays open.
If you sayIt solves it, if God exists.
ThenThat is a large condition, and other Steps take it up.
If you sayI'd rather stay undecided.
ThenThat is an honourable place on a question that has occupied people for twenty-five centuries.

The same in the other books

Translation

He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?

Original · Hebrew

הִגִּ֥יד לְךָ֛ אָדָ֖ם מַה־טּ֑וֹב וּמָֽה־יְהוָ֞ה דּוֹרֵ֣שׁ מִמְּךָ֗ כִּ֣י אִם־עֲשׂ֤וֹת מִשְׁפָּט֙ וְאַ֣הֲבַת חֶ֔סֶד וְהַצְנֵ֥עַ לֶ֖כֶת עִם־אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

Micah · 6:8

World English Bible

Translation

“‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahweh. The stranger who lives as a foreigner with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.

Original · Hebrew

לֹֽא־תִקֹּ֤ם וְלֹֽא־תִטֹּר֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ וְאָֽהַבְתָּ֥ לְרֵעֲךָ֖ כָּמ֑וֹךָ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃ כְּאֶזְרָ֣ח מִכֶּם֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה לָכֶ֜ם הַגֵּ֣ר ׀ הַגָּ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֗ם וְאָהַבְתָּ֥ לוֹ֙ כָּמ֔וֹךָ כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

the Torah (Leviticus) · 19:18, 34

World English Bible

Translation

Depart from evil, and do good. Seek peace, and pursue it. Yahweh’s eyes are toward the righteous. His ears listen to their cry.

Original · Hebrew

ס֣וּר מֵ֭רָע וַעֲשֵׂה־ט֑וֹב בַּקֵּ֖שׁ שָׁל֣וֹם וְרָדְפֵֽהוּ׃ עֵינֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה אֶל־צַדִּיקִ֑ים וְ֝אָזְנָ֗יו אֶל־שַׁוְעָתָֽם׃

the Psalms · 34:14-15

Therefore, whatever you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.

Πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν θέλητε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς· οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 7:12
